layerBlurbs.skin: Body surface, mapped as named anatomical regions.
layerBlurbs.muscles: Skeletal muscles of the muscular system.
layerBlurbs.organs: Internal organs of the visceral systems, including the heart.
layerBlurbs.vessels: Arteries, veins, and lymphatic vessels and nodes.
layerBlurbs.nerves: Central and peripheral nervous system with sense organs.

descriptions.Liver: The body's largest internal organ. It filters blood, produces bile for digestion, and stores energy as glycogen.
descriptions.Stomach: A muscular sac that churns food with acid and enzymes, beginning protein digestion.
descriptions.Kidney: Filters waste from the blood to produce urine, and regulates fluid, salts, and blood pressure.
descriptions.Pancreas: Produces digestive enzymes and the hormones insulin and glucagon that control blood sugar.
descriptions.Gallbladder: Stores and concentrates bile from the liver, releasing it to digest fats.
descriptions.Urinary bladder: A stretchable muscular reservoir that stores urine before it leaves the body.
descriptions.Trachea: The windpipe — a cartilage-ringed airway carrying air between the larynx and the bronchi.
descriptions.Left ventricle: The heart's strongest chamber. It pumps oxygen-rich blood through the aorta to the whole body.
descriptions.Right ventricle: Pumps oxygen-poor blood through the pulmonary trunk to the lungs.
descriptions.Left atrium: Receives oxygen-rich blood returning from the lungs and passes it to the left ventricle.
descriptions.Right atrium: Receives oxygen-poor blood from the body via the great veins.
descriptions.Thyroid gland: A butterfly-shaped gland in the neck that sets the body's metabolic rate.
descriptions.Prostate: A gland surrounding the urethra that produces part of the seminal fluid.
descriptions.Spleen: Filters blood, recycles old red blood cells, and helps fight infection.
descriptions.Duodenum: The first section of the small intestine, where stomach contents meet bile and pancreatic enzymes.
descriptions.Jejunum: The middle section of the small intestine, where most nutrients are absorbed.
descriptions.Oesophagus: A muscular tube that carries swallowed food from the throat to the stomach.
descriptions.Tongue: A muscular organ for taste, chewing, swallowing, and speech.
descriptions.Femur: The thigh bone — the longest and strongest bone in the human body.
descriptions.Humerus: The upper-arm bone, connecting the shoulder to the elbow.
descriptions.Sternum: The breastbone, anchoring the ribs and protecting the heart and lungs.
descriptions.Clavicle: The collarbone, strutting the shoulder away from the ribcage.
descriptions.Scapula: The shoulder blade — a flat triangular bone gliding over the back of the ribcage.
descriptions.Atlas (C1): The first cervical vertebra. It carries the skull and lets you nod your head.
descriptions.Axis (C2): The second cervical vertebra. Its peg lets the atlas pivot, turning the head.
descriptions.Corpus callosum: The great bridge of nerve fibres connecting the brain's two hemispheres.
descriptions.Abdominal aorta: The body's largest artery as it descends through the abdomen, supplying the organs and legs.
descriptions.Pulmonary trunk: The great artery carrying oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle toward the lungs.
descriptions.Superior lobe of left lung: One of the left lung's two lobes, where inhaled air exchanges oxygen with the blood.
descriptions.Superior lobe of right lung: The uppermost of the right lung's three lobes.
descriptions.Vermiform appendix: A small blind-ended tube off the caecum; a reservoir of gut flora with immune tissue.
descriptions.Sartorius: The longest muscle in the body, crossing hip and knee to fold the legs tailor-style.
descriptions.Biceps brachii: The two-headed flexor of the elbow on the front of the upper arm.
descriptions.Rectus abdominis: The paired 'six-pack' muscle flexing the trunk forward.
descriptions.Gluteus maximus: The body's largest muscle, extending the hip in stair-climbing and standing up.
